title: Autoscaler lease-table saturation causing soft reserved capacity loss
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: During a high-churn period on 2026-03-02 morning, several Dedicated customers (notably Acme Health) experienced silent throttles and increased 429s despite apparent reserved pool availability. Root cause analysis shows the autoscaler's in-memory lease table shards were saturating due to tombstone accumulation from rapid create/delete of short-lived reservations. The shard compaction/GC loop failed to keep up under churn, causing the scheduler's free_slot metric to undercount available capacity and reject new reservations (soft capacity loss).

Impact: Intermittent degraded throughput for ~7% of dedicated tenants in eu-west-1 during peak, elevated tail latencies, and customer escalations to Support (SUP-4892). No data plane model degradation observed; degradation was allocation-level and resulted in increased fallback to hosted models for a few tenants.

Root cause details: The lease table is implemented as sharded append-only segments with tombstoning on release. Under heavy churn, the GC process that compacts segments is scheduled by a heuristic (lease_table_gc_interval + tombstone_fraction threshold). A recent change to the lease allocator optimization (ENG-421997) altered the allocation path so that rapid re-allocations left many micro-tombstones and pushed GC below the processing budget when autoscaler leader also performed rebalance computations. This produced three effects: 1) per-shard free_count drift, 2) metric lease_table_free_fraction not reflecting transient reclaimable capacity, and 3) scheduler rejecting requests when global free_count dropped below safety margin.

Short-term mitigation (already applied):
- Increased lease_table_gc_interval aggressiveness and force-triggered compaction on leader change (hotfix deployed 2026-03-03) to reclaim tombstones quickly.
- Temporarily raised reserved-pool soft-thresholds to allow short bursts while compaction completes.
- Deployed a synthetic churn load in canary to validate compaction effectiveness.

Hotfix/Code changes: PR #1287 implements:
- deterministic compaction worker with backpressure awareness (limits CPU impact),
- an additional metric lease_table_pending_tombstones_per_shard and lease_table_free_fraction_override when compaction is in-progress, and
- a scheduler guard that consults compaction_inflight to avoid double-rejecting reservations.

Monitoring & Alerts added:
- alert if lease_table_pending_tombstones_per_shard > 500 for >2m,
- alert if lease_table_free_fraction < 0.15 and compaction_inflight=false,
- dashboard panels for shard-level tombstone counts and compaction latency.

Customer comms and escalation handling:
- Support ticket SUP-4892 opened for Acme Health; on-call engaged and provided interim workarounds (route to hosted fallback and temporary quota bump).
- Incident bridge notes and timeline posted to #incidents and #dedicated-ops.
- CS/AM notified for impacted accounts; follow-up scheduled for postmortem and credit evaluation.

Planned follow-ups / long-term work:
1) Add end-to-end integration tests that simulate high churn reservation patterns and validate compaction under leader rebalance (owner: Marco Liu).
2) Rewrite lease table storage to bounded-size ring buffers with explicit live-count tracking to avoid append-only tombstone growth under churn (RFC to be scheduled; owner: Storage Group).
3) Improve autoscaler leader election handoff to guarantee compaction triggers during leadership transfers (owner: infra-scheduler).
4) Post-incident runbook entry: step-by-step playbook to detect and remediate lease-table saturation, including queries, thresholds, and quick toggles.

Acceptance criteria for closing ticket:
- PR #1287 merged and deployed across eu-west-1 and us-east-1,
- No recurrence over two 7-day high-traffic windows,
- Integration churn test in CI gating autoscaler, and
- Runbook added to ops-runbooks with playbook tested in a fire-drill.
